items.title: 63475_Arnett Cobb oral history interview
items.q: Reuben Phillips was writing for me

ctx.x: I went to Birdland, and I had a graduated contract. I started with so much money a week, and each time I'd go back and get another $100.00 increase over a period of time. So I finally got in there now on one occasion. I'd played opposite many musicians, Dizzy Gillespie, (inaudible) Charlie Parker. I told you he used my rhythm section in there.

But I went in there one time with Willis Jackson, and George Rhodes was writing for me. Reuben Phillips was writing for me, and they keep the scores, and they was giving Willis same arrangement, and I'm trying to miss him, and he's trying to miss me without playing the same thing. I got so mad, boy, and George was with me on bass. I said, 'Man, you ought to be shame of yourself to make more money off the same arrangement you wrote for' -- I'm not lying to you.
